weakest_categories.reason: Identifying the smallest-magnitude change class requires fine quantitative ranking that a frozen-feature classifier cannot recover; near chance among small ratio buckets.
Estimating a numeric change-ratio bucket needs quantitative area reasoning not present in pooled image features.
Comparing which land-cover class changed most requires spatial/area reasoning; slight regression (-0.76 pp) vs baseline.

where_change_model_helped_most: change_to_what (+1.91 pp): naming the post-change land-cover class benefits from BLIP's CDVQA-tuned visual features.
smallest_change (+1.41 pp) and change_ratio (+0.72 pp): small but real gains on the hardest ratio types.
cross_cutting_reasons: Fine quantitative reasoning (ratios, smallest/largest magnitude) is the dominant failure mode - shared with the baseline; a pooled-feature classifier lacks the spatial arithmetic needed.
Domain: trained/evaluated on SECOND 0.1524 m aerial RGB; other sensors/resolutions unproven.
next_experiment_implications: Ratio/counting categories would need spatially-aware features (patch/region tokens) or an auxiliary area estimator, not just pooled embeddings.
A per-question-type router could send binary/semantic questions to cdvqa_transfer and keep deterministic measurement for extent/ratio - a future accuracy-aware improvement.
